history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - Bon (Yungdrung Bon) monastery; keep-or-drop decision needed. Bon is the indigenous Tibetan spiritual tradition predating Buddhism in Tibet, distinct from the four Buddhist schools (notable differences: Bon monastics take a vegetarian vow, and circumambulate counter-clockwise). The original Menri Monastery was founded in Tibet in 1405 by Nyamme Sherab Gyaltsen; after the 1959 uprising, Bonpo lamas gathered in Kullu-Manali, and about 70 families shifted to Dolanji in 1967, registering the Tibetan Bonpo Foundation. The Yungdrung Bon Monastic Centre was founded by Abbot Lungtok Tenpai Nyima, the 33rd Menri Trizin, with Lopon Tenzin Namdak - foundation laid in 1969, completed in 1978. It is the principal Bon monastery outside Tibet and the seat of the Menri Trizin (spiritual head of the Bonpos), housing 200+ monks, a dialectic school with Geshe training, a library, a Bon Children's Home, and the Redna Menling nunnery nearby. CSV town corrected: Dolanji village (~15 km from Solan), not Solan town. Coordinates come from the centre's place-listing record and are approximate - verify on the ground.

name: Menri Monastery (Dolanji Bon Monastery)
town_description: Dolanji is a village in Solan district, Himachal Pradesh, about 15 km from Solan town on the Narag-Sarahan road (via Oachghat). It sits in pine forest in the Shivalik foothills and is best known for its Bon monastery.
tradition: Bon (Yungdrung Bon) - indigenous Tibetan tradition, distinct from Buddhism; NOT Hindu

travel.railway: Solan railway station on the Kalka-Shimla narrow-gauge line (~25 km, verify); Kalka also serves the area
travel.road: Via Oachghat on the Solan-Rajgarh road, then a diversion onto the Narag-Sarahan road; about a 40-minute drive from Solan

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Losar (Tibetan New Year) and the Cham dance festival are the main events
visitor_information.opening_hours: 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM daily (per the centre's business listing; verify locally)
